newsitem.title: MEXICO: Vitro CFO sees return to growth in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Vitro CFO sees return to growth in 1998.

text.p: Mexican glassmaker Vitro SA expects to return to a growth path in 1998 after recovering from the sale of its U.S. subsidiary Anchor Glass, the company CFO told Reuters.
The company's first aim will be to generate value for its shareholders and reduce indebtedness in 1997.
"Once we have done those two things, we will begin to thoroughly look into a growth path as of 1998 for the group," Vitro Chief Financial Officer Jose Antonio Lopez said.
The sale last week of its bankrupt Anchor Glass subsidiary will saddle Vitro with a heavy loss of 3.063 billion pesos to be charged against the group's 1996 earnings, according to company estimates.

Lopez said the company would base growth on its core business activities, glass containers and flat glass. He noted, however, that glass containers were facing increasing competition from substitutes such as PET and aluminium.
"Now and in future years we will have more competition. It is up to us to make glass competitive, using its great advantages, such as recycling," he said.
Vitro will channel most of its investment in 1997 into flat glass production, including $77 million for expanding production by 40 percent at a float-glass plant in Mexico City, Lopez added.
Lopez also rejected criticism of Vitro's branching out into consumer goods, saying its Household Goods division would be a key prop for future growth.
"This division exported $50 million in 1995, $100 million in 1996, and will export $180 million in 1997. We see a great future for it," he said.
